deviations: Volatility 25th/75th percentiles taken over the party-level estimation sample (N=430) using Stata-style percentiles (R quantile type 2); the paper says only 'in the sample'.
Ethnic party coded as ethnic > 0.5 (strict majority of expert coders report ethnic/linguistic linkages).

Ideological extremism uses the supplied extremist2 variable (per the codebook, vote-share-weighted absolute distance from the country mean left-right placement); extremist party at distance 3, moderate at 0.

Country covariates coded as: pluralty and pr dummies (mixed omitted); closed-list (cl==1) and open-list (cl==2) dummies (non-list omitted); mdmh; polity; demsys; system as a 3-level factor (presidential omitted); gdppc; gini; ethfrac. Party covariates: partysize, unions, business, religious.
Table 1 sample is complete cases on both outcomes, volatility, all covariates, ethnic and extremist2 (430 parties, 75 countries), so every panel uses the same sample.
notes: Table 1: OLS with country-clustered (HC1/CR1) SEs; the quantities are linear combinations of coefficients (beta*(p75-p25) for the volatility differences; b_group + b_interaction*vol for group differences), which do not depend on the covariate values. Table 2: rdrobust (local linear, triangular kernel, mserd bandwidths) on the open-seat sample (dlameduck_runs==0), running variable mv_incparty, cutoff 0; conventional point estimate reported. attempt-1 was an exploratory run (no RESULT lines). attempt-2: docker ran before the script file existed, because the sandbox guard refused the command that would have written it; Docker created an empty directory at script.R, nothing ran, and there was no output. attempt-2/script.R is an empty placeholder recording that. The codebook.pdf inside the mount was read for variable definitions. The authors' .do/.R scripts were not opened.
